chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Yaqoub ibn Salim, from Al-Muthanna, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Yaqoub (peace be upon him) had a caller who would call out every morning from his house for a distance of a farsakh: 'Indeed, whoever desires the morning meal, let him come to the house of Yaqoub.' And when it was evening, he would call out: 'Indeed, whoever desires the evening meal, let him come to the house of Yaqoub.'
ai.seo_question: What was the practice of Prophet Yaqoub regarding providing food to the people?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical generosity of Prophet Yaqoub (Jacob), peace be upon him, by detailing his systematic provision of morning and evening meals to the community. It serves as a foundational model for *sadaqah* (charity) and communal dining in Shia tradition, emphasizing the Prophet's role in ensuring no one went hungry. The specific mention of 'morning' and 'evening' meals underscores the consistency and accessibility of his hospitality.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Asbat, from Yaqoub Bin salim, from Al Musny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Yaqoubasws had a caller for himas who used to call out every lunchtime from hisas house up to a Farsakh, ‘Indeed! The one who wants the lunch, so let him come to the house of Yaqoubas!’ And when it was evening he would call out, ‘Indeed! The one who wants the dinner, so let him come to the house of Yaqoubas!’
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Ali from Ali ibn Asbat from Ya’qub ibn Salim from al-Muthanna’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said

Ya’qub, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, had an announcer who every morning announced from his house to three miles, ‘Those who want lunch can come to the house of Ya’qub.’ In the evening the announcement said, ’Those who want dinner can come to the house of Ya’qub.’”
